aspect_ratio_witnesses.conclusion: area Ln and a single fixed-point count each lose information retained by the ordered two-clock geometry and its divisor history

global_positive_domain.search_domain: 1<=L,n<=24, ordered by increasing area; all positive divisors of each area included

nondegenerate_domain.search_domain: 2<=L,n<=24, ordered by increasing area; all eligible divisors of each area included

nonzero_exact_period_domain.search_domain: 2<=L,n<=24 with at least one witness cell having P_L(n)>0

same_fixed_count_different_primitive_str.statement: both fixed-point counts are 16, but n=3 has 15 exact-period points and five primitive cycles whereas n=6 has none

even_length_control.purpose: explicit non-squarefree sentinel for the kernel-gcd theorem

kernel_gcd_theorem.kernel_lemma: for monic f and h over a field, dim ker(m_h:k[x]/(f)->k[x]/(f))=deg gcd(f,h)
kernel_gcd_theorem.kernel_proof: writing f=g f_1 and h=g h_1 with gcd(f_1,h_1)=1, the annihilation condition f|hq is equivalent to f_1|q; the residue classes f_1 r with deg r<deg g form a basis
kernel_gcd_theorem.laurent_clearance: x^n((x+x^{-1})^n-1)=(x^2+1)^n+x^n in characteristic two; multiplication by x^n is invertible modulo x^L+1
kernel_gcd_theorem.non_squarefree_scope: the proof uses ideal divisibility, not distinct roots, so it includes every even L for which x^L+1 may be non-squarefree

mobius_orbit_theorem.integrality_reason: F_L acts on a finite set; exact-period-n points are partitioned into temporal cycles of size n
mobius_orbit_theorem.point_cycle_boundary: Fix(L,n), P_L(n), and C_L(n) are distinct quantities and are never interchanged

nonclaims: a thermodynamic or infinite-volume limit of the two-clock table
that area alone determines spatiotemporal periodic geometry
an arithmetic Euler product or local factorization
a target divisor, functional equation, or counting-law match
Route-B authorization or a solution of the larger program

progress_and_boundary.progress: constructs an all-size exact spatiotemporal periodic table for a local linear cellular automaton and separates points from primitive temporal cycles
progress_and_boundary.route_a_obstruction: the family has intrinsic finite-volume periodic structure but no single frozen circumference, clock, or target determinant
progress_and_boundary.two_clock_obstruction: collapsing (L,n) to area loses aspect ratio, while one fixed count loses divisor-history information

source_lock.allowed_data: the Rule-90 local rule and computations derived from it
source_lock.clock: the ordered pair (spatial circumference L, temporal iterate n)
source_lock.cutoff: the theorem is all L,n>=1; the replay ledger is 1<=L,n<=24
source_lock.determinant_convention: no single-variable determinant is asserted; the frozen object is the exact two-clock fixed-point table
source_lock.forbidden_data: external prime or zero tables, arithmetic/local factors, root numbers, automorphy claims, and Route-B inputs
source_lock.normalization: Fix(L,n) counts labeled spatial configurations fixed by F_L^n; exact-period points are divided by n only after temporal Mobius inversion
source_lock.object: Rule-90 on the cyclic binary lattice R_L=F_2[x,x^{-1}]/(x^L-1), with F_L multiplication by a=x+x^{-1}
source_lock.precision: exact F_2 polynomial arithmetic and exact integers

spatiotemporal_torus.bijection: a torus is uniquely determined by its row j=0, and closure in time is exactly F_L^n u=u
spatiotemporal_torus.equations: u_(i,j+1)=u_(i-1,j)+u_(i+1,j) in F_2 with i mod L and j mod n
spatiotemporal_torus.torus_count: the number of labeled L-by-n tori is Fix(L,n)
